# Acquaintance Party ticketing — project context

Project context and rules live in `context/`:
- `context/RULES.md` — coding & implementation rules, security-critical patterns
- `context/ARCHITECTURE.md` — stack, folder structure, data flow
- `context/DESIGN.md` — theme tokens, per-surface visual treatment
- `context/PRD.md` — product requirements, scope, current status
- `context/SCHEMA.md` — database schema

Read the relevant file(s) before non-trivial work. These are the fast-reference
layer; the full reasoning behind each decision lives in
`docs/superpowers/specs/` (the design spec) and `docs/superpowers/plans/` (the
implementation plan) — read those when a `context/` file says "see the spec"
or when you need the *why*, not just the *what*.

## Event runway

Under two weeks from the design spec's date (2026-08-30) to the event. Every
design and scope decision in this repo already optimizes for that — see
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-30-acquaintance-party-ticketing-design.md`
§Constraints. Don't propose scope that assumes more time than that.

## Surface priority

Not every screen gets the same design effort. Landing, checkout, and the
raffle projector are the themed public surfaces. The door scanner and admin
screens are function-first — semantic color only, dense, no theme accent. See
`context/DESIGN.md` for the full breakdown and why it's a hard rule, not a
preference.

## Plan before implementing

No feature or non-trivial modification starts with an edit. Investigate the
existing code, present the approach and the files it touches, then implement.
Use plan mode for anything multi-file or design-bearing; skip the ceremony
for a genuinely trivial, fully-specified change.

## Security-critical patterns — read before touching auth, payments, or storage

- `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` bypasses every RLS policy. It is read only in
  `src/lib/supabase/admin.ts`, guarded by a `server-only` import. Never let
  it reach a file under `"use client"`. See `context/RULES.md`.
- Anonymous users get **zero** RLS policies on `registrations` or `scans`.
  Every public read/write goes through a server action holding the
  service-role key. If you're about to write an `anon` policy, stop — that's
  the wrong layer.
- The ticket QR renders as pure black on pure white with a quiet zone,
  always. This is a phone-camera constraint, not a style choice — see
  `context/DESIGN.md`.

## Git commits

Author commits as the user only. Do not add a `Co-Authored-By: Claude` (or
any AI) trailer, or a `Claude-Session` link.

## Explaining things

Write for a reader who is skimming, not studying. Plain words over jargon,
short sentences, the answer first. Name the concrete file, column, or number
instead of describing it abstractly. Don't pad with restatement or a recap of
what was just said.
